summary.text: 兴 is the standardized simplified form of 興. The traditional character depicts people lifting an object together; the object’s identity is uncertain. Its modern meaning includes “flourish” and “prosper.”

formation.text: The traditional graph 興 is commonly analyzed as a semantic construction depicting several hands jointly lifting an object. The received account parses it as 舁 plus 同, explaining the action as people working together; this reading does not establish the object’s identity or the graph’s original design. A proposed analysis assigning 型 a phonetic role is not supported by the formation evidence. 兴 is the standardized simplified form of 興, described as adapted from its cursive form.

history.text: The supplied account describes 兴 as adapted from the cursive form of 興, and Unihan identifies it as the standardized simplified counterpart. The evidence here does not give a detailed dated sequence for that graphic change.
The curated seal-script image is a modern redraw of the received 興 form, not an excavated inscription, so it cannot show the appearance or chronology of early forms.

uncertainties.text: The traditional character is interpreted as people jointly lifting an object, but the object and its original spoken name are uncertain. The received 舁-plus-同 explanation is an old analysis, not settled proof of the graph’s first design.
One account proposes 型 as a phonetic element, but the formation sources cited here do not establish that component or role.
Early inscriptional and manuscript uses are reported, but their dates do not establish a complete sequence of the character’s meanings.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in oracle-bone and later textual contexts
senses.text: Early contexts are reported with a sense of rising or getting up; one oracle-bone use is described in connection with illness improving. This does not prove that rising was the character’s original meaning, and the chronology is incomplete.

senses.period: bronze-inscription and manuscript contexts; precise dates unresolved here
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions and manuscript contexts are reported using the character for raising or mobilizing troops. Their chronological relationship to the rising sense is not established.
The character has recorded senses of flourishing and prosperity, also reflected in common modern glosses. The evidence does not establish a specific path from rising or mobilizing to this sense.

limitations.text: The reported senses and examples do not establish a dated sequence or show which early use, if any, was the original meaning.

overview.text: 兴 is the simplified form of 興. The traditional graph is interpreted as several people lifting an object together, though the object is uncertain. Today, 兴 commonly means “flourish” or “prosper.”

relationships.text: 興 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 兴; the graph is described as adapted from 興’s cursive form.
